SILENCE: EU-Mexico trade deal / GM shifts production from China to Mexico
May 18–21, 2026 | 🔴

📰 All 27 EU states approved a modernized trade deal with Mexico. First EU-Mexico summit in 11 years set for May 22 in Mexico City with von der Leyen and Costa. Bilateral trade projected to increase 35% over five years — a direct counterweight to US dependence.

Meanwhile, GM announced it's shifting Chevrolet Aveo and Groove assembly from China to Mexico — 80,000 vehicles/year by 2030, part of $1B in investment announced alongside Sheinbaum. The Aveo is GM's top seller in Mexico with 60,000+ sold in 2025.

US mainstream coverage of either story: near zero. Mexico's biggest trade diversification in a decade and a factory line gained from China — neither made the front page of a single major US outlet.

THE GUARDIAN: 'If you keep looking we will kill you': death stalks those searching for Mexico's disappeared
May 20, 2026 | 🟡

📰 The Guardian profiles Mexico's searcher collectives — mostly women looking for 113,000+ disappeared since 2010. Twelve searchers killed in 2025. Over 4,500 clandestine graves found, 6,200+ bodies recovered. The human cost is real and devastating.

What's missing: Sheinbaum's government expanded federal resources for search collectives and created a new National Search Commission framework. The piece presents the crisis without the policy response — a pattern when US/UK outlets cover Mexico's hardest stories.

NBC NEWS / CFR: Mexico's long war: Drugs, crime and the cartels
May 19, 2026 | 🔴

📰 NBC republishes a CFR backgrounder calling Mexico's security situation a "long war" with "limited success" — right before World Cup kickoff. One sentence on US drug demand. Zero on US gun exports arming the cartels.

The US is framed as the generous partner providing "billions in security assistance." Mexico is the perpetual failure. López Obrador dismissed as merely echoing predecessors. Sheinbaum's approach "does little." Structural drivers — US demand, US weapons, US-pushed militarization — erased from the narrative.

• US role: "billions of dollars in security and counternarcotics assistance"
• Mexico's role: "waging a deadly battle for two decades, with limited success"
• Gun trade mentioned as cartel activity — never sourced back to the US

FOREIGN AFFAIRS: Why Mexico's Cartels Are So Hard to Defeat
May 20, 2026 | 🟡

📰 Foreign Affairs runs 5,000 words asking why cartels are "so hard to defeat" — acknowledges Mexico posted its biggest single-year peace gain on record (22.7% homicide drop) then spends the rest explaining why it doesn't really count.

Article credits Sheinbaum's intelligence-driven strategy but frames every advance as insufficient. Record seizures, high-value operations, institutional reforms — none survive the piece's built-in skepticism. Two decades of US-designed militarized drug war failed, but somehow Mexico's government owns the outcome.

• "Seizures alone do not dismantle drug networks"
• "Investigative agencies botched the job at El Mencho's hideout"
• "If Mexico's war on drugs is to achieve more than fleeting military victories"

May 15 – 21, 2026

1. FOREIGN AFFAIRS — "Why Mexico's Cartels Are So Hard to Defeat" (🟡) — acknowledges record homicide drop, spends 5,000 words explaining why it doesn't count
2. NBC/CFR — "Mexico's long war: Drugs, crime and the cartels" (🔴) — evergreen warzone backgrounder republished before World Cup; one sentence on US demand, zero on US guns
3. THE GUARDIAN — "If you keep looking we will kill you" (🟡) — real disappeared-searcher crisis, omits government's expanded search resources
4. SILENCE — EU-Mexico trade deal / GM shifts production from China to Mexico (🔴) — biggest trade diversification in a decade, near-zero US coverage
MEXICO'S ECONOMY GROWS 0.3% IN APRIL — Industry bounces back after tariff shock. Services advancing 0.7% annually keep the broader economy moving forward.
30+ NATIONS CONDEMN BEN-GVIR FOR MOCKING BOUND FLOTILLA ACTIVISTS — Video shows 430 activists bound, kneeling, forced to listen to anthem. Multiple governments summoned Israeli ambassadors.
RUBIO TELLS CUBANS THE US ISN'T RESPONSIBLE FOR THEIR CRISIS — His offer: 100M in aid but only if Cuba changes its political system. That's a bribe dressed up as charity.
CUBA CONDEMNS DESPICABLE US INDICTMENT OF RAUL CASTRO — DOJ charges stem from 1996 incident Cuba calls self-defense after 25+ airspace violations
FGR: SINALOA CARTEL INFILTRATED 8 MORELOS MUNICIPALITIES THROUGH CAMPAIGN FINANCING — Mayor arrested, UIF froze 32 accounts tied to cartel operator El Barbas
